author: Elastic
attributes.description: Detects shells or scripting interpreters launched from a parent command line that contains common LLM prompt-injection or jailbreak language. Attackers (or malicious content ingested by an agent) use instruction-override, DAN/developer- mode, system-prompt extraction, and safety-filter bypass phrasing to coerce GenAI coding agents and automation wrappers into running attacker-chosen commands. When that injected text reaches a child shell or interpreter, it is a strong signal that untrusted prompt content is crossing into local code execution, enabling credential theft, data exfiltration, persistence, or further tool abuse under the user's privileges.
false_positives: Approved red-team, evaluation, or detection-engineering tests that deliberately include jailbreak strings (such as DAN or "ignore previous instructions") in prompts or regex experiments run through GenAI agent shells. Exclude known lab hosts or lower severity after validation.
Documentation that mentions "developer mode", "jailbreak", or "without restrictions" in a non-adversarial context. Review the full parent and child command lines before escalating.
attributes.name: Potential Prompt Injection Coercing Shell Execution
attributes.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating Potential Prompt Injection Coercing Shell Execution

A shell or scripting interpreter started with a parent command line that matched common jailbreak /
instruction-override language (for example "ignore previous instructions", DAN/"Do Anything Now", or
"bypass the safety filter"). This can indicate a GenAI agent or wrapper being coerced by untrusted prompt
text into local code execution. The alert is a content heuristic on command-line text — confirm whether the
strings are adversarial injection versus security testing or documentation.

### Possible investigation steps

- Review `process.parent.command_line` and `process.command_line` for the matched jailbreak phrases and the
  surrounding payload (paths, URLs, credentials, download/execute patterns).
- Identify the parent process tree (`process.parent.name`, `process.parent.executable`) and whether it is a
  known GenAI client (Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Windsurf, etc.) or a shell-snapshot wrapper.
- Correlate with other GenAI-related alerts on the same `host.id` / `user.name` in the same window
  (unsafe permission bypass, suspicious shell via GenAI client, credential-path access).
- Check recent GenAI config or MCP changes and any outbound network activity from the same process tree.
- Determine whether the activity aligns with approved red-team / detection-engineering work.

### False positive analysis

- Approved red-team, evaluation, or detection-engineering tests that deliberately include jailbreak
  strings. Exclude known lab hosts or users.
- Claude Code / similar agents wrap user commands in `zsh -c` / `bash -c` shell-snapshots, so the phrase may
  appear in both parent and child command lines for a single user action.

### Response and remediation

- If not an approved test, isolate the host/user session, review the GenAI conversation or agent history for
  the injection source, and rotate credentials accessible to that user.
- Audit GenAI tool configs, MCP servers, and skills loaded during the session.
- Block or restrict the responsible agent/automation if compromise or successful coercion is confirmed.
attributes.query:
process where event.type == "start" and event.action in ("exec", "start") and
(
  process.name like~ (
    "bash", "dash", "sh", "tcsh", "csh", "zsh", "ksh", "fish", "busybox", "mksh",
    "timeout", "env", "bun",
    "bash.exe", "sh.exe", "env.exe", "timeout.exe", "bun.exe",
    "cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh", "pwsh.exe", "powershell_ise.exe",
    "osascript",
    "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "mshta.exe"
  ) or
  ?process.pe.original_file_name in (
    "Cmd.Exe", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll", "powershell_ise.EXE",
    "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "MSHTA.EXE"
  ) or
  process.name like~ (
    ".*",
    "python*", "perl*", "php*", "ruby*", "lua*", "node*", "deno*"
  )
) and
process.parent.command_line : (
  "*ignore previous instructions*", "*ignore prior instructions*",
  "*ignore all previous*", "*ignore your previous*",
  "*ignore the content policy*",
  "*disregard previous instructions*", "*disregard prior instructions*",
  "*disregard all previous*",
  "*disregard your system instructions*", "*disregard the system instructions*",
  "*disregard all system instructions*",
  "*disregard your developer instructions*", "*disregard the developer instructions*",
  "*dan mode*", "*stan mode*", "*aim mode*", "*dude mode*",
  "*do anything now*", "*you are dan*",
  "*bypass the safety*", "*bypass the safety filter*", "*bypass safety filter*",
  "*bypass the content filter*", "*bypass content filter*",
  "*bypass the content policy*", "*bypass content policy*",
  "*bypass your guidelines*",
  "*no safety filter*", "*no content restriction*",
  "*without any restrictions*", "*without your restrictions*",
  "*without content restrictions*", "*without safety restrictions*",
  "*unrestricted ai*", "*unrestricted developer mode*",
  "*jailbreak the*", "*jailbreak mode *", "*jailbreak mode,*", "*jailbreak mode.*",
  "*jailbreak mode!*", "*jailbreak prompt*",
  "*forget everything you were told*", "*forget previous instructions*",
  "*you are now in*developer mode*",
  "*override your safety*",
  "*hidden system prompt*",
  "*reveal your system prompt*", "*reveal the system prompt*",
  "*dump your system prompt*", "*dump the system prompt*",
  "*print your system prompt*", "*print the system prompt*",
  "*show your system prompt*", "*show the system prompt*",
  "*override your system prompt*", "*override the system prompt*"
)
